key_insight: A stable Galerkin reduced-order model combined with an extended Kalman filter can accurately reconstruct Rayleigh-Bénard convection states, even from sparse velocity-only measurements.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables practical state estimation and sensor planning for thermal-fluid systems, supporting reduced-cost monitoring of flows where full-field measurements are unavailable.
method: Build a nonlinear ROM from controllability modes of the linearized Boussinesq equations.
Use the ROM as the EKF prediction model and assimilate synthetic DNS data as observations.
Apply the Kalman gain to rank sensors and progressively remove the least informative ones.
evidence_signal: Across periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic regimes, the method tracks energetic modes well and achieves time-averaged reconstruction errors below 14% for velocity and 9% for temperature.
watch_item: Performance depends on the fidelity and stability of the chosen ROM and on having measurements representative enough for the EKF to correct the full state.
paper_title: State estimation of Rayleigh-Bénard convection with reduced-order models
